title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a conformal sphere (the Riemann sphere P^1(C) with its conformal structure). G = Aut_conf(X) is the full conformal group, including anti-holomorphic maps. So G = PGL_2(C) ⋊ Z/2, with identity component G^+ = PSL_2(C). A 'normalized spherical Riemannian metric' is a round metric of constant curvature 1, compatible with the conformal structure, normalized to total area 1. These metrics form one G-orbit R(X), and the stabilizer of one of them is O(3). So R(X) ≅ G/O(3) ≅ PSL_2(C)/SO(3) = hyperbolic 3-space H^3. The next page records that R(X) is homogeneous of dimension 3.

In this picture, an H-invariant normalized spherical metric is the same thing as a fixed point of H acting on H^3.

Statement (H a compact subgroup of G):
(a) An H-invariant metric always exists. This is the Cartan fixed-point theorem for a compact group acting on a CAT(0)/Hadamard space. Equivalently, every compact subgroup lies in a maximal compact subgroup, a conjugate of O(3).
(b) The invariant metric is unique iff X^H = ∅, i.e. H fixes no point of the sphere at infinity.
(c) Suppose X^H ≠ ∅ and H ≠ {1}. Then either card X^H = 2, or H = {1, σ} with σ an inversion (an anti-conformal reflection in a circle).
- Case card X^H = 2. Put H^+ = H ∩ G^+. Then X^H = X^{H^+}, and H^+ lies in a unique compact torus T, the rotations about the axis joining the two fixed points. The invariant metrics correspond bijectively to the orbits of T in X \ X^H, i.e. the 'parallels' (≅ R_{>0}). Each parallel defines the metric for which it is the equator. In H^3 terms, the fixed set is the geodesic joining the two fixed points.
- Case H = {1, σ}. The invariant metrics correspond to (X \ X^σ)/σ. This is one of the two discs bounded by the fixed circle, i.e. a hyperbolic plane. A point p corresponds to the round metric with poles p and σ(p). The fixed set in H^3 is the totally geodesic plane bounded by the circle.

Purpose. This classifies the H-fixed locus R(X)^H, which serves the 'Récapitulation' on the next page. There Grothendieck assigns a canonical compatible metric to every conformal surface without boundary except C and P^1. For P^1 he needs to know when a canonical metric can be chosen invariantly under a given symmetry group. This is part of his 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' (cutting and gluing conformal surfaces with canonical metrics). The previous page computes normalizers of tori N = T ⋊ {1, σ}, with σz = a z̄, to identify fixed circles.

The margin notes 'à vérifier' and asks for a more direct proof of the statements via the group action on spherical metrics.
errors: No mathematical error found. The case analysis matches the classification of fixed sets of compact groups on H^3: all of H^3 (H trivial), a plane (H a single circle-reflection), a geodesic (H fixes two boundary points, X^H of cardinality 2), or a point (X^H empty).

Gap 1: uniqueness ⇒ X^H = ∅ needs an argument. If H fixes an interior point and a boundary point, it fixes the whole geodesic through them, so the fixed set is not a single point. Grothendieck flags the statement as 'à vérifier' and gives no proof.
Gap 2: the hypothesis should read 'compact' (or relatively compact, as on the next page). The inserted word above Aut_conf is uncertain.
Gap 3: in case 1 it is implicit that H^+ ≠ {1}. This holds because a group containing only one reflection falls under case 2, and two reflections compose to a nontrivial rotation.

ideas.what: Space of normalized round metrics on the conformal sphere as a 3-dimensional homogeneous space G/O(3) (= hyperbolic 3-space); invariant metrics are fixed points of H
ideas.modern_name: Identification of conformal round metrics on S^2 with points of H^3 (barycenter / conformal-natural-extension picture)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Poincaré extension); used systematically by Thurston and Douady–Earle (1986)

ideas.what: Existence of an invariant round metric for compact subgroups, and uniqueness iff no fixed point on the sphere
ideas.modern_name: Cartan fixed point theorem; fixed sets of compact subgroups of Isom(H^3)

ideas.what: Explicit parametrization of the fixed loci: parallels of the torus T (geodesic case) and points of a half-sphere (X\X^σ)/σ (plane case)
ideas.modern_name: Totally geodesic fixed sets in H^3 identified via boundary data

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks for a direct (presumably intrinsic, non-computational) proof of the classification of invariant spherical metrics. The modern answer is exactly the H^3 / Cartan fixed-point picture, which he does not state explicitly. This is a small loose end within his larger project of canonical metrics for conformal surgery, not a new result.
missed.quote: NB Il faudrait aussi : trouver une démonstration directe ... sur les métriques sphériques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It documents that his 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' (related to the Esquisse and the cut-and-glue description of moduli) relied on equivariant canonical metrics. That aspect of the project is little discussed, but the mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page states correct but classical facts: invariant round metrics on the Riemann sphere under compact subgroups, which amounts to fixed points in H^3. It is of interest mainly as documentation of the 1983-84 conformal surgery project, not as new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The word inserted under 'Aut_conf(X) = G' is uncertain ('fermé[?]'). It may instead be 'connexe' or similar; the hypothesis actually used is 'compact'.
The bracketed sentence probably reads '[chacune des orbites de T dans X \ X^H définit une telle métrique]'. The relevant group is T (or H^+ acting through T); the orbits of T are the parallels.
Margin: the deciphered phrase 'action de Aut G[?]' is doubtful. The sense is a request for a direct proof concerning invariant spherical metrics.
